Issued at 340 AM EST Wed Nov 11 2026

Water vapor imagery early this morning depicts a sharp upper level 
short wave across western Iowa. An eastern Pacific jet streak 
progressing through the base of this trough will induce sfc 
cyclogenesis across southeast Iowa/west central Illinois this 
morning into this afternoon as sfc reflection reaches east central 
Indiana by this evening. Low level winds will back this afternoon in 
advance of this trough and strengthening low level flow in this 
deepening phase will allow for northward push to low/mid level theta-
e boundary currently displaced to the south-southwest of the local 
area. Given strongly forced nature to this setup and respectable low-
mid level RH developing, have maintained likely rain shower PoPs 
from west to east this afternoon into this evening. While there is a 
period of stronger advection this afternoon, the short duration of 
this advection will make it difficult to realize any appreciable 
instability. Moistening low and mid levels combined with maintenance 
of some drier sub-cloud air could provide some favorable 
theta-e differentials for a period of gusty winds associated 
with the showers (perhaps SPS level gusts over 40 mph) late this
afternoon into early this evening. Maturing nature to low level
baroclinic zone and sharpness of low/mid level trough may 
support a deformation- band of rain into this evening. Otherwise
today, the warm advection regime will provide above normal 
temperatures despite the increased cloud over with highs from 
the mid 50s north to low to mid 60s south. 

Passage of the initial upper trough this evening will set the stage 
for favorable storm track for several additional disturbances in 
northerly upper flow to bring reinforcing shots of cold air 
into the southern Great Lakes region later tonight into Friday. 
Lake effect rain showers are expected to start as early as later
this evening as shallow lake induced instability develops. 
Initially this lake effect may manifest as cellular convective 
mode given some synoptic low level troughing expected across the
southern Great Lakes and shallow nature to instability depth. 
The more impressive synoptic trough will dive south across the 
southern Great Lakes on Thursday, with a period of isolated to 
scattered rain showers area-wide as this trough drops south. In 
the wake of this disturbance, flow profiles should begin to 
align more favorably down long-axis of Lake Michigan for a more 
dominant single band event Thursday night into Friday. Lake 
temperatures remain above normal, generally in the 80-90 
percentile for mid November. While this will aid in lake induced
instability, it does also raise questions of low level thermal 
modification downwind of Lake Michigan and influences on precip 
types. Have generally followed idea of most of higher-res 
guidance in greater potential of snow overnight a bit away from 
the lakeshore where this modification of low level thermals will
not be as dramatic. After 06Z Thursday night, depth of cold air
should overcome marginal low level wet bulbs for a period of 
mainly snow shower ptypes especially away from the lakeshore. 
There are also some indications that another synoptic mid/upper 
trough could be rotating cyclonically across the western Great 
Lakes which could provide some increased lift to nudge areas to 
snow ptype for a brief window closer to the lakeshore also. Of 
course, plenty of uncertainties as to exact low level flow 
trajectories and timing of this mid level short waves, but 
confidence is increasing in the potential of some localized 
inland slushy accumulations of an inch or two across portions of
NW Indiana and possibly far SW Lower Michigan early Friday 
morning. 

Loss of stronger synoptic forcing during the day Thursday combined 
with diurnal tendencies should take p-types back to rain during the 
day as low level flow trajectories remain favorable for an extended 
period of lake effect precipitation. Another upper level spoke to 
the broad upper level negative height anomaly is progged to dive 
south to the southern Great Lakes Friday night into early Saturday. 
Low level gradient will be a bit weaker by this time which could 
support some land breeze sharpening of lake effect banding. The main 
question for Friday night/Saturday AM will be potential of enough 
low level airmass modification to keep p-types as mainly rain.
One wildcard will be if stronger low level lift induced by 
stronger convergence with possible land breeze enhancement can 
be enough to changeover precip types for a time. Depth of lake 
induced instability does appear to start to diminish during the
overnight hours Friday night. There is also some question as to
whether favored area of banding may shift west of the local 
area briefly Friday night in response to the stronger synoptic 
forcing.

Lake effect rain showers continue Saturday but should be in a 
diminishing state Saturday afternoon as inversion heights
